note:
The driver: an injected hs under plain lua, ten arms over create_space's reporting paths and call counts. Covers AC-01.1's four behaviours and AC-01.5, AC-01.6 and AC-01.7, which are ST0032's AC-03.3, AC-03.4 and AC-03.5 recreated here verbatim: descope records the move on the source thread and creates nothing on the destination, so they had to be written rather than transferred. AC-01.2 was withdrawn as subsumed by AC-01.5, which now exists on the same thread, so that withdrawal reads correctly.

SEEN RED, TEN TIMES OVER, before ever being called green. Every one of the driver's ten arms was reddened by at least one landed one-line mutation to a copy of the engine, across slots YYCYT8 and CQXAX4: arms 2, 3 and 4 by the creating call retried on a lagging count (fa0a7b58's regression, caught from three directions), arm 3 also alone by the final-failure path not consulting made (bf6e5f08), arm 4 by the overshoot going unreported, arm 6 by the vanished display being retried, arm 0 by is_user_space's accepted string, arm 1 alone by the success readback off by one, arm 5 by the retry budget cut to one, arm 7 by the count-before guard disabled, arm 8 by the already-failed guard disabled, and arm 9 by the per-display lookup made global. Each mutation was proven to have landed on exactly one line before it was run. The full evidence, with every line number and the defect each mutation recreates, is on AT-01.3. This row records red FIRST because a driver written against code that already works can pass while asserting nothing, and four of this thread's ten arms had no recorded defect behind them to suggest they worked at all.

GREEN against the unmutated engine: 45 checks passed, 0 failed, exit 0, run as `lua opt/arngz/test/engine_test.lua opt/arngz/lib/arngz.lua` under Lua 5.5.1 in slot YYCYT8, and green again inside slot XYJSED, where engine.bats ran the driver against the unmutated engine and found no failures and more than no passes. NOT in CQXAX4, which ran only the six mutants and no control: an earlier wording of this note said it did, and that was wrong, written from the plan for pass 2 rather than from its script. The engine was not changed to make this pass: arngz.lua and plan.lua are byte-identical to 5d7bfe37, the head ST0032's own arms ran green at, which utilz-vc verified independently. WHAT THIS GREEN IS AND IS NOT: it proves the DRIVER detects the classes of defect it was built for, and says nothing yet about exec_create_space itself, which no suite has ever reached. Not covered here: Lua 5.4, both passes having run under 5.5.1 alone while CI has a 5.4 leg; and the bats caller engine.bats, which this row does not run, so AC-01.4 and AT-01.2 stand open on a separate booking.
